static_traits.name: Li Peiqi
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet received psychological counseling; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, cooperative and self-reflective; neutral-to-anxious tone, tending to repeatedly recall negative events and self-evaluate in absolutist language

basic_info.main_problem: After missing the doll I wanted to buy at the last antique fair, I felt extremely disappointed and sad, and regarded the whole experience as awful; this disappointment and catastrophizing thinking persist and recur, affecting my daily life.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to identify and challenge one's catastrophizing and extreme thinking, explore evidence and restructure cognitions, practice more realistic balanced views, thus improving mental health and daily functioning.
growth_experiences: In childhood, had an emotional attachment to dolls and kept some as a collection; the doll at this antique exhibition evoked the emotional connection of childhood, so missing out on that doll was subjectively experienced as a 'personal failure'.
Never before experienced such intense disappointment and negative thinking; this antique-show incident became a significant trigger.

special_situations.event: At an antique exhibition, a beloved doll is bought by someone else
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not achieved my self-set goal (must buy that doll), it equals I failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Judging experiences by all-or-nothing standards, absolutizing the day's goal to prove one's ability
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I messed up; I cannot even do such a simple thing well

special_situations.event: In the weeks after the antique exhibition ended, repeatedly replays the details whenever thinking of the event
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one key mistake occurs, the whole experience has no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Through repeatedly recalling and picking out negative details tries to gain explanation and a sense of control, while avoiding discussing feelings deeply with friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That day was a complete failure, with nothing worth remembering

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do a little bit wrong, the entire time afterward will be ruined
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Evaluating outcomes catastrophically and blaming oneself, reinforcing the harsh inner rule of 'avoiding mistakes'

special_situations.event: When encountering small setbacks or unsatisfactory moments in life
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure means I always fail, proving my ability is insufficient
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses attention on evidence of failure to confirm self-judgment, ignoring the positive aspects
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do anything well; things always go wrong

core_conflict.wish: Longing to confirm one's self-worth and ability by achieving important goals, to be seen and recognized
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and not being recognized, worrying about being seen as not good enough
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control through self-blame and absolutist standards, avoiding exposure of vulnerability and disappointment

object_relations.self_representation: A failure who cannot do things well
object_relations.object_representation: Others who are faster and more capable and will take away opportunities

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites Li Peiqi to review the missed doll or a recent small slip, and inquires about her attribution of responsibility
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to interpret occasional external events as one's own insufficient ability, taking full responsibility (transference: blaming failure on oneself)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Language dominated by self-blame, using absolutist expressions (e.g. 'it is all my fault for messing up'); low tone, little discussion of external factors.

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly self-evaluating in absolutist language during counseling (e.g. 'I cannot do anything well')
More likely to focus first on negative evidence, difficult to spontaneously acknowledge the positive
Not yet discussing one's emotions and disappointment deeply with friends in daily life

exception_events.target_problem: After unsatisfactory events, Li Peiqi usually catastrophizes and views the whole experience as failure, thus feeling low and ruminating persistently.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On the antique-show day, although missing the desired doll, she still enjoyed viewing other antiques, interacting with people, and found and bought several small items she liked; this differed from the old reaction of 'the whole day was a failure'.
exception_events.reason: Different situations and clues: pleasant interactions and other gains that day (seeing other desired antiques, meeting interesting people, finding small items); these positive experiences provided evidence for a non-catastrophizing narrative.

positive_force: Able to identify and state the day's positive aspects in retrospect (finding small items, meeting interesting people)
Willing to practice more balanced perspectives and reality testing
Has some social support (several friends to talk to)
negative_force: Catastrophizing tendencies and all-or-nothing thinking patterns
Habits of mental filtering and negating the positive
Ruminative pattern of repeatedly replaying events
Self-denial and attributing failure entirely to oneself

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing evaluation and ruminative thinking (repeatedly replaying negative events, engaging in self-denial in all-or-nothing ways)
antecedent: Missing a desired doll at an antique fair
Recalling afterward and focusing on negative details
target_behavior.core_reason: Interpreting not yet achieving the goal as 'personal failure', driven by all-or-nothing thinking, mental filtering, overgeneralization and other cognitive biases, maintaining a 'sense of control' over outcomes through self-blame.
target_behavior.function: Escaping directly facing disappointment and uncertainty, gaining temporary interpretation and control through self-blame and catastrophizing; also trying to prevent future mistakes with harsh standards.
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and increased anxiety, difficulty seeing the positive side, affecting daily life and well-being.
